name: telegram-messaging-mcp
description: Telegram (messaging): me, send, list_inbound. Every tool maps to a documented endpoint.

platform_mcp_telegram_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_TELEGRAM_TOKEN
platform_mcp_telegram_token.description: Bot token from @BotFather. It is part of the URL path: 'All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME' (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#making-requests).

tools.name: me
tools.description: getMe returns the bot's User object (id, is_bot, first_name, username).

tools.name: send
tools.description: `to` is the chat_id ('Unique identifier for the target chat or username of the target channel'). `subject` and `channel` are ignored. Bots cannot message a user who has not started them. message_id is an integer within the chat (the sent Message is under raw).

tools.name: list_inbound
tools.description: Long-polling queue, not a paged inbox: getUpdates returns the pending updates (kept up to 24 hours) and 'will not work if an outgoing webhook is set up'. This tool never sends `offset`, so it does not confirm/consume updates and repeated calls return the same pending updates; `page` and `since` are ignored and next_page is not meaningful. Updates that are not messages have no text; chat and sender ids are integers under raw.message.chat.id / raw.message.from.id.
